intro: Skyline Drive is a residential street in the Garibaldi Highlands. Residents raised concerns about speeding.

The District of Squamish put Skyline Drive, from Garibaldi Way to The Boulevard, on its 2026 traffic calming list. The plan is one raised crosswalk and updated signs. A raised crosswalk is a crosswalk built up like a wide, flat speed bump.

The District says the contractor expects to build it on October 29 and 30, 2026, weather permitting. The District is also looking at other changes for Skyline Drive in a future year (as of October 2026).

timeline.what: A traffic calming request was logged for Skyline Drive, Braemar Drive to The Boulevard.
Another request was logged for Skyline Drive, Garibaldi Way to Braemar Drive.
Council endorsed a new Traffic Calming Policy for Squamish.
Both Skyline Drive sections appeared on the District's list of eligible locations, with the Braemar to The Boulevard section ranked second.
The District said the raised crosswalk would be built October 29 and 30.

points: A raised crosswalk slows drivers right where people cross, and the request has been on file since 2019.
Updated signs make the speed limit and the crossing clearer to drivers.
Raised crosswalks slow everyone, including buses and emergency vehicles.
Some would prefer enforcement or signs alone, without changing the road.

questions.a: Yes, as of late October 2026. The District expects the work on October 29 and 30, weather permitting.

questions.q: Will there be more changes on Skyline Drive?
questions.a: The District says it is working to identify other possible improvements for a future year.

questions.q: How does the District decide where traffic calming goes?
questions.a: It reviews resident requests against speed and volume data, road type, collision history and emergency routes, then ranks the eligible sites.
